email.body1:
Kelly, saw Casepoint went to Thoma Bravo, landed a 5-year Air Force contract, and cleared CMMC Level 2 and FedRAMP High.

That momentum in regulated and government markets usually means more accounts in play than the team can cover before reps work the new openings, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Casepoint off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Kelly, quick follow-up for Casepoint.

Under new ownership with fresh government credentials, the target usually grows faster than business development can cover. Most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Casepoint needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Kelly, last bit of proof for Casepoint.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Casepoint's reply rate likely compares to other legaltech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Kelly, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority right after the Thoma Bravo deal, no problem at all. Integration is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a regulated-markets motion? I will tailor it to Casepoint either way.
